questions.prompt: If you wanted to quantify the aerosol radiative forcing including atmospheric adjustments in a global model (i.e., the effective radiative forcing, or ERF), which model would you use and why?
questions.answer: You would ideally use an ensemble of 5-year simulations of an atmosphere-only climate model. The aerosol forcing including atmospheric adjustments is defined as the change in net downward radiative flux at the top of atmosphere caused by a radiative perturbation to the Earth including adjustments to the atmosphere without a change in surface temperature (which elminates the option of using a fully coupled atmosphere-ocean model). The adjustments to the atmosphere occur on timescales of days to months, so a 5-year simulation is sufficient to capture these effects. A single 5-year simulation would be insufficient because the internal variability of the climate system would make it difficult to distinguish the aerosol forcing from natural variability. An ensemble of simulations allows you to average over this internal variability and obtain a more robust estimate of the aerosol forcing. A chemical transport model would not be appropriate because it does not allow for the atmosphericadjustments. A 20-year run of an atmosphere-only climate model would be unnecessary because the adjustments to the atmosphere occur on much shorter timescales. Nudged models are often used for quantifing ERFs. Nudging is used to keep the model close to observed meteorology, which can be useful for comparing with observations, but it is not necessary for quantifying ERFs, and such simulations have the disadvantage that some adjustments may not be properly represented.
options: A chemical transport model because the 3-D fields of atmospheric motion are fully specified and unaffected by the aerosol, so you can easily compare simulations with different aerosol emissions.
A 20-year run of an atmosphere-only climate model because the aerosol effects on the atmosphere that are relevant to aerosol forcing take at least a decade to occur.
An ensemble of 5-year simulations of an atmosphere-only climate model because the…
A coupled atmosphere-ocean climate model because the full effects of aerosol on surface temperatures needs to be simulated for the adjustments to be realistic.

questions.prompt: How many quantities would a model need to transport if it represented aerosol as a sectional particle size distribution with size 20 bins, with each bin carrying the chemical species sulfate, nitrate and black carbon?
questions.answer: A model would need to transport 80 quantities. This is because there are 20 bins, and each bin carries 3 chemical species, so the total number of chemical tracers is 20 * 3 = 60. However, to specify the size distribution, the model also needs to transport the total number of particles in each bin, which adds an additional 20 quantities. Therefore, the total number of quantities that need to be transported is 60 + 20 = 80.

questions.prompt: How many quantities would a model need to transport if it represented aerosol as 3 lognormal particle size distributions of varying number concentration and size but constant shape, with each bin carrying the chemical species sulfate, nitrate and black carbon?
questions.answer: A model would need to transport 3 quantities for each of the 3 lognormal particle size distributions, totaling 3 * 3 = 9 quantities. However, to specify the size distribution, the model also needs to transport the total number of particles in each distribution, which adds an additional 3 quantities. Therefore, the total number of quantities that need to be transported is 9 + 3 = 12.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is always true of a two-moment cloud microphysics model?
questions.answer: A two-moment cloud microphysics model can simulate an evolving particle size distribution, but some properties of the distribution still need to be specified. The two moments typically represent the total number of particles and the total mass of particles, which allows the model to simulate changes in the size distribution over time. However, with just two moments, other properties of the distribution may still need to be specified or assumed. For example, a lognormal aerosol distribution is fully specified by three quantities (mean, standard deviation, and total number), so a two-moment model does not fully capture all properties. A two-moment model does not always simulate particle number and mass, as it depends on how the moments are defined. A two-moment model is not always necessary to calculate aerosol-cloud interaction forcing, as some single-moment models can also simulate the effect of aerosol on droplet number.
options: It is needed to calculate aerosol-cloud interaction forcing because a single-moment model cannot calculate the effect of aerosol on droplet number.
It always simulates particle number and mass.
It can simulate an evolving particle size distribution, but some properties of the distribution still need to be specified.
It can simulate all the properties of a particle size distribution.

questions.prompt: What is the value of π (pi)?
questions.answerInfo: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, so it is dimensionless.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are greenhouse gases?
questions.answer: The greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor. Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
